blocks.intro: Most shower valves in Mokena are from the 1990s and 2000s, and parts are usually still available.

items.body: On most valves from this era, a new cartridge fixes drips and temperature swings without opening the wall.
A small leak can stain the ceiling below. We find the source before opening anything.
They drain to an [ejector pump](/mokena/ejector-pump), so a slow basement shower may be a pump problem.
Many Mokena bathrooms have one-piece tub and shower units. A crack in the base can leak into the ceiling below, and we can tell you whether it's the valve, the drain or the unit.

items.q: Why does my shower turn hot or cold when someone flushes?
items.answer: The pressure-balancing cartridge in the valve is worn out. Replacing it usually fixes the problem.

items.q: Can you fix a shower leak without removing tile?
items.answer: Usually. Most valve repairs are done through the trim plate. Leaks in the pan or behind the tile may need more work.

items.q: Can you replace my shower valve?
items.answer: Yes. We can replace an old valve with a newer pressure-balancing or thermostatic valve.

items.q: Why is my shower spray so weak?
items.preview: Usually a clogged showerhead or screen.
items.answer: Usually mineral buildup in the showerhead or the valve screen. Cleaning or replacing them restores the flow.

items.q: Can you replace a tub with a walk-in shower?
items.preview: We handle the plumbing for the conversion.
items.answer: Yes, we handle the plumbing: moving the drain, installing the new valve and connecting the fixtures. Tile and glass are done by your remodeler.

items.q: Can you add a second showerhead?
items.answer: Often, if the valve and supply can handle the flow.

items.q: How much does shower repair cost in Mokena?
items.preview: It depends on the problem. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what's wrong and how we reach it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
